The longest river in the world is the Nile River.

To understand inflation theory in cosmology, imagine you are looking at a photograph of a vast, empty desert. Now, imagine that just a fraction of a second before that photo was taken, the entire desert was compressed into a space no larger than a grain of sand. Inflation theory proposes that this tiny speck expanded exponentially and incredibly fast, stretching out to become the massive universe we see today.

The analogy of blowing up a balloon is helpful, but it needs a slight adjustment to be perfectly accurate. When you blow up a balloon, the rubber stretches, and dots drawn on the surface move away from each other. However, the dots themselves don't grow; the space between them does. Similarly, during inflation, space itself stretched rapidly. It wasn't that galaxies were flying through space faster than light; rather, the "fabric" of space between them was expanding so quickly that the distance between them increased at a rate that exceeded the speed of light. This explains how the universe could become so uniform and large in such a short time, much like how a small, wrinkled balloon can quickly become a large, smooth sphere when inflated rapidly.
